correctness.rationale: All 65,536 subsets of each sixteen-vertex graph have two agreeing independent face predicates; the resulting complete face vectors and Hasse incidences are exhaustively reconstructed by the embedded checker. There are 639 and 543 disjoint element-matching pairs, respectively, and directed Hasse topological sorts visit all 1336 and 1192 nonempty faces, proving acyclicity. Exactly one critical vertex and 57 (respectively 105) critical 3-cells remain, no other critical cells; the discrete Morse CW models are forced to be wedges of those numbers of 3-spheres over the integers, not merely mod-two homology. Direct mod-two simplicial boundary calculations independently give ranks 57 and 105 in degree 3 and zero elsewhere.

originality.rationale: Published higher-independence theorems inspected in primary arXiv full texts address explicitly different graph families or require chordality; both graphs here contain induced chordless squares. Research-record searches using both graph aliases, the induced-maximum-degree-one and dissociation formulations, explicit ranks and related complexes yielded as closest ordinary first-independence, neighborhood/Čech and original-edge two-matching results. Their statements do not imply the present threshold-two homotopy types. Unindexed literature and the inaccessible full text of a closest first-stage comparison remain residual risks. No partition-based uniqueness inference is used.
residual_risks: Equivalent work absent from searched indices may exist; search absence alone does not prove originality.

value.rationale: The two graph objects exhaust the naturally classified strongly regular parameter set (16,6,2,2); they share all local parameters but have unequal higher-independence homotopy invariants at the first genuinely nonordinary threshold. Exact integral sphere-wedge types, not just f-vectors or finite Betti tables, make this a motivated comparative classification and demonstrate parameter-insensitivity of a graph-derived topological construction. This is distinct from merely repeating the already studied ordinary independence classification.
